question: On dev items (N=5, four domains), patching the dissoc source's residual into the base at the question tokens, the template after the question (final), the last two tokens (last) or question+final, one layer at a time (every 4th layer) and over the early/mid/transit windows, does the base answer move to the identity, position or value prediction, and at which depth?
why_it_matters: Explains the "around" route (C2: the lens reads RL's bridge but cannot write it). At layers 44-52 copying C's question-token residual flips RL 98-100% while the lens direction flips 0% (EXPERIMENTS rows 27, 52). position => the lookup is steered by a binding/positional pointer the lens cannot express (H-pointer; C2 explained); identity => the bridge's identity (or a lexical key) in a non-lens code (H-word); value => by 44-52 the answer is already fetched, so read-without-write there is a timing effect, not an "around" code (H-value). Sets the windows for d3_main_27b.

hypotheses.H-pointer: RL, final (and last) at the transit window 44-52: position >= 50%, identity <= 20%, value <= 20%; RR position <= 10% (identity >= 50%); DL position >= 50%
hypotheses.H-value: RL final/last transit: value >= 50% (the source's digit, absent from the base)
hypotheses.H-none: RL final transit changes the answer < 20% (would contradict the suite's copy flips; design mismatch)
hypotheses.prior: Agent prior (before any run): question group identity at layers <= 28 under every hypothesis (the cue words are patched); at 44-52 on final/last: value 0.4, position 0.3, identity 0.3. Mixing Mechanisms predicts position mainly for first/last slots and identity (lexical) / reflexive in the middle: reported by slot.

decision_rule: Fixed before the run (scripts/pointer_swap.py docstring). Per cell (family x group x layer/window, dissoc source, pooled over domains, Wilson 95%): interpretable iff 1 - share(none) has lower bound >= 0.20 and the same control's change rate has upper bound <= 0.10 (else "none" / "damage"); verdict X in {identity, position, value} (RR: identity, position) iff X's lower bound exceeds the other two upper bounds and the chance bar (the rand control's upper bound for X; the per-digit context rate); else "mixed". Primary cell: RL, final, transit. The pilot decides nothing by itself: it fixes the main run's layer range (the layers where RL final changes >= 20%) and is reported with its n.
controls: same source (q_s = q_b at the same slot, same digit, rest of the context reshuffled and redigited): every hypothesis predicts the base answer; rules out damage from patching a residual computed on another context
rand: seeded random direction at the dissoc patch's per-position norm: rules out generic disruption picking a context digit (chance bar for identity/position)
other: another domain's item (same family), its residual at the same distance from the prompt end, rescaled to the dissoc norm: realistic-activation null; also probes a domain-general positional code
context digits predicted by no hypothesis (N=5: 2 per item): the per-digit chance rate inside the same runs
base into base at the middle layer (no-op) and layer-0 all-position patch (reproduces the source): hook checks
n: 15 scenes per domain x 4 domains = 60 per family (180 cases), dev e5f0
notes: Reads per case: 3 checks + 16 layers x 4 groups x 2 (dissoc, same) + 8 layers x 4 x 2 (rand, other) + 3 windows x 4 x 2 = 219 -> 39.4k edited reads. Throughput: suite_split map_A8_v1 (27B, faster box) 76.8k reads in 1205 s = 64/s; read_write layers_v1 50k in 571 s = 87/s; the A100 PCIe at ~1/3 of that -> ~22/s -> 30 min + load. command: uv run python scripts/early_push.py run --name d4_push_v1 --why "D4: is a hard early lens push (layers 16-28, 4-16x the copy's norm) the same as editing the input word, or a write of the intermediate? Decides whether layers_v1's early RL flips contradict C2" --n 60
examples_command: uv run python scripts/early_push.py examples --name d4_push_v1
question: On Qwen3.6-27B at layers 16-28, does the lens push v_X - v_I that flips RL 35-61% and BL 24-44% act like putting X's word into the question (agreeing item by item with the text edits, not depending on the cue positions, moving BL as much as RL) or like writing the intermediate variable (agreeing with C's own in-transit state)?
why_it_matters: C2 says the lens cannot write a lookup-used bridge where the model carries it. layers_v1 found early pushes that flip RL (and BL, whose bridge the lens barely reads). H-inject keeps C2 (the early flips are input edits, upstream of where the bridge is carried); H-write kills C2 as stated (RL is writable, just early). It also tells the "around" route story whether early lens directions act on words or on variables.

hypotheses.H-inject: K1 dk = kappa(P*, E-insert) - kappa(P*, W-copy*) > 0 with CI above 0 (e.g. +0.2 to +0.4); flips(nb) >= flips(a)/2 (pushing everything but the subject phrase keeps >= half the effect; layers_v1's r-push, a subset of nb for RL, already flips RL 35-61%); BL within 15 points of RL at P* (e.g. 40% vs 50%); K4 cos(P*_b, E-name) - cos(P*_b, E-cue) > 0 at the final positions (layers 32-40); E-unrelated flips < 10%
hypotheses.H-write: dk < 0 with CI below 0; flips(b) >> flips(nb) and flips(nb) < flips(a)/2; BL < RL - 15 points (BL's bridge is not lens-readable at the question, so a lens write lands less); K4 < 0; P*_b's transit projection on C's copy delta at 44-52 >= E-name's

decision_rule: Fixed in scripts/early_push.py's docstring and manifest before the run. P* = the lens push at subset a (whole question region + template) whose RL flip rate is nearest 50% over layers 16/20/24/28/band x scales 4/8/16; W-copy* per family = C's copy at 32-48 nearest 50%; emb* = the embedding push nearest 50% on RL. K1 (RL): CI of dk above 0 inject-like, below 0 write-like; counts only if the gate passes (kappa(emb*, E-insert) - kappa(emb*, W-copy*) CI above 0 on RL). K2 (RL, P*'s layer and scale): inject-like if flips(nb) - flips(a)/2 has CI above 0; write-like if that CI is below 0 and flips(b) - flips(nb) has CI above 0. K3: flips(BL) - flips(RL) at P*, paired by scene: inject-like if CI lower bound > -0.15, write-like if upper bound < -0.15. Verdict: "push behaves like an input-word edit" if >= 2 of K1-K3 inject-like and none write-like; "push writes the intermediate" if >= 2 write-like and none inject-like; otherwise mixed. K4/K5, countries, BR/RR, O, text loss reported, not decisive. Item bootstrap, 2000 resamples, seed 0.
controls: random direction at the same per-position norm for every lens push and embedding push (rules out any big push)
r-subset push = layers_v1's push on the same items (replication anchor; summary.json replication)
C's copy at r at 16-28 (the 0% anchor) and at 32-48 (W-copy*: the model's own in-transit variable, graded)
edited-input activation patch (Biran et al. 2024 back-patching): the C run's residual at a, at 16-28, raw and at the push's per-token norm
embedding push e_X - e_I and e_X at the subject phrase: the "edit the input word" limit; its kappa pattern is the gate for K1
E-unrelated: X named in an unrelated context sentence (does merely mentioning X move the answer?)
O (off-path prompt) under the push and WikiText next-token loss under the push vs random: collateral damage
countries R/B (bridge read and written by the lens at 44-52): the same measures where a lens write is known to work
n: 60 per family (BL, BR, RL, RR on the same 60 scenes, the first 60 of map_A8_v1 = a subset of layers_v1's 80; countries R, B 60 each)
notes: Timing: ~200 edited reads per item (150 lens/random pushes, 16 patches, 9 copies, 8 embedding pushes, 15 O pushes, 4 text edits) x 360 items = ~72k reads; at ~22 reads/s (A100 assumption shared by the D-jobs: 1/3 of the H200's 64/s; layers_v1 itself did 49,920 reads in 571 s = 87/s on the sprint box) ~55 min, + 27B load ~3 min, + per-item state metrics and Python overhead ~2 s/item ~12 min, + plain-text loss (4 pairs, 16 rows, 121 conditions, full sequences) ~3 min: ~1.2 h. Outputs are appended scene by scene (suite scenes first, countries last), so a stopped run keeps every finished scene. If tonight's budget is tight, --n 50 saves ~10 min. Layers 16 and 20 fall before the first third of depth (21.3 of 64: the paper's pre-workspace band), 24 and 28 after it. Results: results/early_push/d4_push_v1/.

command: uv run python scripts/statement_positions.py map --name d1_map_v1 --why "D1: where the lookup reads the bridge, statement positions vs question tokens (position-set x layer copy map)" --n 32 --layers 0 8 16 24 28 32 34 36 38 40 44 48 52 60
examples_command: uv run python scripts/statement_positions.py examples --name d1_map_v1
question: Where, by position set (the bridge's binding statement, its word, the other bindings, the lookup rows, the whole context, the question, its words, the template tail) and layer, does each family carry its bridge, i.e. where does copying C's residual into the clean run give X's answer?
why_it_matters: Every "around" measure (copy split, lens read/write) was taken at the question tokens only. For bound bridges the bridge is stated in the context and only referred to in the question (lens reads BL there 7%; question copy moves BL only 10-17% at 32-40). If BL's bridge is still in transit at the statement positions at layers 32-40, the "around" result for lookups (claim C2: memory through the J-space, prompt lookups around it) may be a location artefact; d1_parts_v1 / d1_rw_v1 then test the J-space there. If BL has left the statements by 32, H-loc's location premise fails at the question-token layers.

hypotheses.H-loc: BL (and BLR): a statement set (bind_bridge, bridge_word, lookup_x or context) is in transit (C copy flips >= 50%, above controls) at >= 1 of layers 32-40, while the question set flips <= 20% there (map_A8_v1: 5-10%)
hypotheses.H-early-handoff: BL's statement sets stop being in transit before layer 32 (last transit layer <= 28) and no set flips >= 50% at 32-40 except context (the bridge is spread over the lookup rows / question words)
hypotheses.prior: Prior (Dan's agent, before any run): H-loc 0.55 (the question copy only takes over BL at 48-52, so the bridge must sit somewhere upstream at 32-40), H-early-handoff 0.45. Sanity expectations: every B family's bridge_word copy flips >= 90% at layer 0; RL/RR/R statement copies exact no-ops; countries B question set in transit by layer 40 (control_split map_v1: 81% at 40).

decision_rule: Fixed before the run (module docstring of scripts/statement_positions.py). Transit cell: C's copy gives X's answer in >= 50% of cases and its Wilson 95% lower bound exceeds the upper bound of every control's change rate (O's copy where non-zero; the random-direction copy at the same per-position norms); zero-delta cases count as unchanged. Handoff per family and statement set = the last transit layer. H-loc's location premise holds for BL if any statement set is in transit at a layer in [32, 44); it fails if none is. Run invalid if: identity changes the top token in any case, all0 misses C's top token in > 2% of cases, any causality violation (a predicted-zero cell with a non-zero delta), or read-vs-greedy agreement < 99%.
controls: O (off-path counterfactual: X's and Z's lockers / friends / rows / holders swapped) copied at the same cell, where its delta is non-zero: rules out "any change to these positions moves the answer"
random direction per position at the C copy's norm (same cell): rules out a norm / disruption effect, and is the only control at the binding statements (O is exactly zero there)
cue-only families (RL, RR, countries R): C's statement copies are exact no-ops by construction (verified numerically on every case and layer; read on the first 5 cases)
identity copy and C-at-every-position-at-layer-0 per case (hook checks); read vs greedy on the first 10 cases per family
paired readers: BL/BR (BLR/BRL) share scenes, so their statement-position patches are identical
n: 32 per family (BL, BR, RL, RR, BLR, BRL from suite_split map_A8_v1's case list; countries R, B from control_split map_v1's), i.e. read_write's case selection (first n per family)
notes: Time: 67,996 edited reads (plan stage on the 27B tokenizer: 14 layers x 9 sets x C / O / random, zero cells skipped). Throughput on the A100 PCIe assumed 22 reads/s = the H200 runs in EXPERIMENTS.md (map_A8_v1 76,800 reads in 1,205 s = 64/s; read_write layers_v1 87/s) divided by ~3 (bf16 312 vs 989 TFLOPs, 1.9 vs 4.8 TB/s) -> 0.86 h + 3 recording forwards per case + load ~ 0.95 h; d1_smoke_27b's ledger time recalibrates it. Layers: every 8th outside the handoff window, every 2nd in 28-40 (the question-token measures sit at 32-40; the question copy takes over BL at 44-52), the coarse grid's 32/36/40 for the parts / readwrite cells. n=32 sized to the night's 2.5 h D1 budget (Wilson half-width ~0.17 at 50%); a full run (n=80, every layer 32-52) is 4.2 h.

command: uv run python scripts/statement_positions.py parts --name d1_parts_v1 --map d1_map_v1 --why "D1: at the transit cells (statement positions vs question), is the copy's effect carried by its J-space part?" --lo 32 --sets bind_bridge bridge_word lookup_x context question
examples_command: uv run python scripts/statement_positions.py examples --name d1_parts_v1
question: Where the bridge is in transit at layers 32-40 (d1_map_v1's transit cells), does the J-space part of C's copy carry more of its effect than its share of the copy predicts, at the statement positions as at the question tokens?
why_it_matters: Kills or supports the location-artefact reading of claim C2's "prompt lookups go around the J-space". At the statements BL and BR receive the identical patch (the context precedes the question), so a BL-BR concentration difference there isolates what the lookup reads from the same representation.

hypotheses.H-loc: at a BL (or BLR) statement set in transit at 32-40: J-space concentration lower bound > 1.2 and above the random-dictionary null's upper bound (countries at the question tokens: 2.5-2.9); BR minus BL concentration at the same cells within +-0.3
hypotheses.H-around: at every BL statement set in transit at 32-40: concentration upper bound < 1.0 (as at the question tokens: 0.3-0.4) with not_jspace - jspace > 0; BR (and countries B) at the same sets > 1.2; BR minus BL > 0.5
hypotheses.prior: Prior (Dan's agent): H-around 0.5, H-loc 0.25, inconclusive / empty cells 0.25. Reasons: the J-space part of the question-token copy never flipped any suite family; the bridge word at its own statement is a token the lens reads easily, which could favour H-loc at bridge_word only.

decision_rule: Fixed before the run (module docstring). Per family, set, primary window (layers 32/36/40 among the transit cells): inside if the J-space concentration (case bootstrap 95%) lower bound > 1.2 and above rand_omp's upper bound; around if the upper bound < 1.0 and not_jspace - jspace > 0 (paired bootstrap lower bound); else inconclusive (suite_split's 2.0 rule reported as verdict_strict). J-space half of D1: H-loc if any BL/BLR statement set is inside; H-around if all are around and the positive control (countries B, else BR) is inside at the same set; around without a passing positive control is not interpretable; no BL statement cell in transit at 32-40 = H-loc's location premise fails (reported, nothing to split).
controls: each part along a random direction at the same per-position norms (its null)
rand_omp: the same 25-atom OMP over a random dictionary (the fitting null for concentration)
jspace_matched / lens2_matched: equal-sized, equally aligned pieces of the copy
jspace_wo_own: the J-space part after the bridge's and X's own lens vectors are projected out (is it the word?)
O's full copy at the same cell; positive control: countries B (recall-used, lens-writable) at the same sets
n: up to 32 per family (d1_map_v1's cases), only families with transit cells
notes: Cells depend on the map. Time per cell ~1.1 s on the A100 (16 reads at ~22/s plus three 25-atom OMPs over ~200k letter-token vectors, fp32); expected ~4 cells per bound-family case and ~1 per cue-only case (~800 cells, 0.3 h); worst case (5 sets x 3 layers in every case) 1.2 h. One layer's dictionaries (two [letters, 5120] fp32 maps, ~8 GB) at a time next to the 27B (layer-major loop).

command: uv run python scripts/statement_positions.py readwrite --name d1_rw_v1 --map d1_map_v1 --parts d1_parts_v1 --why "D1: at the transit cells, does the J-lens read the bridge and does its direction write it?" --lo 32 --sets bind_bridge bridge_word lookup_x context question
examples_command: uv run python scripts/statement_positions.py examples --name d1_rw_v1
question: At the cells where the bridge is in transit at layers 32-40, does the J-lens read it, and does pushing v_X - v_I (0.5-16x the copy's per-position norm) write X, as it does for countries at the question tokens?
why_it_matters: The lens-write half of D1's decision. "Read without write" (RL read 95%, written <= 3% at 32-40) is the strongest "around" evidence; if the lookup-used bound bridge is written by the lens where it is stated, the around result is a location artefact (H-loc); if it resists there too, "around" holds wherever the bridge is in transit (H-around).

hypotheses.H-pointer: RL final/last transit (44-52): position >= 50% [Wilson lower bound > identity and value upper bounds], RR position <= 10%, DL position >= 50%; by slot: position strongest for first/last, weaker in the middle
hypotheses.H-word: RL final/last transit: identity >= 50%, position <= 20%, value <= 20%
hypotheses.H-value: RL final/last transit: value >= 50%; last group value earlier (lower layer) than final
hypotheses.prior: Agent prior: value 0.4, position 0.3, identity 0.3 (to be updated by the pilot before enqueuing).

decision_rule: As d3_pilot_27b (scripts/pointer_swap.py docstring), applied to main items: primary cell RL x final x transit window (44-52) x dissoc, pooled over domains; supported hypothesis = the verdict (position -> H-pointer, identity -> H-word, value -> H-value; none/damage/mixed -> inconclusive). Secondary, reported not decisive: the same rule for group last and both, per layer, per domain, per queried slot (first/middle/last), DL and RR. A verdict that holds in fewer than 3 of 4 domains is reported as domain-dependent.
controls: same source (no-op under every hypothesis): damage
rand (matched-norm random direction): chance bar
other (another domain's item at matched norm): realistic null / domain-general positional code
context digits predicted by no hypothesis: per-digit chance inside the runs
self no-op and layer-0 all-position reproduction: hook checks (run invalid if either < 100% top agreement)
n: 50 scenes per domain x 2 domains (animals, elements) = 100 per family (RL, DL, RR), main N=5
notes: d3_pilot_27b came out 'damage' in every cell, including layer 0 where nothing changes, because its n was 34 per family (months and planets gave 2 eligible scenes each) and the rule asks the 'same' control's Wilson upper bound to be <= 0.10, which needs n >= 35 even at 0 changes (3.84 / (n + 3.84)). This version applies the pre-registered competence gate (a domain x family cell enters iff its clean Wilson lower bound >= 0.85, d3_competence_27b): months RL (46%), planets RR (55%) and planets RL (lower bound 0.84) fail, so only domains passing in all three families are used, and n is raised so the rule can pass. Controls, decision rule and hypotheses unchanged. Timing: d3_pilot_27b ran 102 cases x 16 layers in 601 s (37 reads/s); this run is 300 cases x 23 layers, about 45 min.

command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py manifest --name d3_levels_animals_27b --set dev --levels e3f0 e5f0 e5f4 --domains animals --n 60 --layer-step 4 --competence d3_competence_27b --why "D3 levels on animals: does the split change with 3 statements, or with filler sentences between the statements?" && uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py run --name d3_levels_animals_27b

question: Same patch as d3_pilot_27b (dev items, every 4th layer, question / final / last / question+final, plus the early/mid/transit windows), on the two other dev levels: N=3 statements (e3f0) and N=5 statements with 4 filler sentences woven in (e5f4; the filler layout is the same in base and source). Does the RL split between identity, position and value change against the pilot's e5f0?
why_it_matters: Tests whether the pilot's outcome is specific to 5 adjacent statements. Mixing Mechanisms (Gur-Arieh et al. 2025) predicts the positional route dominates more with fewer entities (N=3). Filler between the statements moves them to other token positions and breaks their adjacency: a pointer that survives it indexes statements, not a fixed neighbourhood. Limitation: the filler layout is shared by base and source, so this does not separate statement order from absolute token offset (that needs an offset-shift variant, not built).

hypotheses.H-robust: RL final/last at the transit window: the pilot's winning outcome keeps its share at e5f4 within 0.15
hypotheses.H-contiguity: the winning outcome's share drops by more than 0.15 with filler (e5f4 vs e5f0)

context digits predicted by no hypothesis (N=5: 2 per item): the per-digit chance rate inside the same runs
base into base at the middle layer (no-op) and layer-0 all-position patch (reproduces the source): hook checks
n: 60 scenes per level (e3f0, e5f0, e5f4), animals only (the only domain passing the gate at every level), dev items

title: D3 alias gate: can the 27B look up statements written in French/Spanish/German or with the chemical symbol?
command: uv run python scripts/alias_pointer_v1.py manifest --set main dev --name alias_competence_27b --limit 200 --why "D3 alias gate: can the 27B look up a statement that names the entity in French/Spanish/German (animals) or by its chemical symbol (elements), on the same scenes as statements in English, every alt and control prompt and each step alone?" && uv run python scripts/alias_pointer_v1.py competence --name alias_competence_27b
examples_command: uv run python scripts/alias_pointer_v1.py examples --name alias_competence_27b
figures_command: uv run python scripts/alias_pointer_v1.py figures --name alias_competence_27b
question: On alias_pointer_v1 (pointer_v1's scenes; the statements in English, or naming the entity in French/Spanish/German for animals and by the chemical symbol for elements; the question always English), does Qwen3.6-27B answer the org prompt, the alt prompt, the two control prompts and each step alone (cue -> entity; the lookup with the entity named or the recalled fact; the other form -> English name) for memory → prompt, named → prompt and memory → memory?
why_it_matters: Gate for the alias patching run (pointer_swap on data/alias_pointer_v1). In pointer_v1 every statement repeats the word the model recalls ("cow"), so matching by that word and matching by meaning look the same. D3's first night (UNVERIFIED) found that after the question, at layers 44-50, memory → prompt carries the statement slot more often than the entity (29% vs 9%). If the 27B can look up statements that do not contain the recalled word, the same patch on this data asks whether that slot pointer (and the smaller entity share) survives when the statement is in another language or uses a symbol: answer of bridge alt's statement with French/Spanish/German statements => the lookup matches by meaning, not by the token the J-lens reads; answer at the same statement slot in every form => a positional pointer that ignores the surface form; entity share only with English statements => a lexical key. A failed gate for memory → prompt with named → prompt passing is itself a result: a recalled bridge cannot find a statement that does not repeat its word.

hypotheses.H-meaning: statements in French/Spanish/German: named → prompt >= 95% and memory → prompt >= 90% (org prompt), each within 5 points of statements in English on the same scenes; the other form -> English name step >= 95%
hypotheses.H-symbol: statements with the chemical symbol: named → prompt >= 90%, memory → prompt >= 85% (pointer_v1 elements, memory → prompt in English: 94% [88, 97])
hypotheses.H-lexical-crutch: memory → prompt with another form < 80% while named → prompt with it >= 90% and memory → prompt in English >= 95%
hypotheses.H-alias-unknown: the other form -> English name step < 90% for some entities (porc, pollo; He read as a pronoun, C or N as letters): those items drop out of the usable set; the gate can still pass
hypotheses.prior: Agent prior (written before any run): H-meaning 0.6 (the suite's translated-word family is answered by the 27B); H-symbol 0.5; H-lexical-crutch 0.25; H-alias-unknown 0.4. Statements in English: >= 95% in every animals cell; elements as pointer_v1 (memory → prompt 94%).

decision_rule: Fixed before the run (scripts/alias_pointer_v1.py docstring, "Gate"). Per domain on main (first 200 scenes per file): the other form enters the patching run iff the org prompt's Wilson 95% lower bound >= 0.80 in both memory → prompt and named → prompt, the statements-in-English cells of that domain pass pointer_v1's rule (lower bound >= 0.85), and >= 35 scenes are usable (every prompt of every family right) in both forms. Usable per item = every prompt right (org, alt, both controls, the steps alone). Report the answer read vs greedy agreement (must be >= 99%) and the paired-by-scene counts (both right / English only / other form only / neither). Dev cells (3 and 5 statements, 60 scenes) are a pilot, never the gate.
controls: statements in English on the same scenes (paired): separates the surface form from scene difficulty
each step alone (cue -> entity; the lookup with the entity named or the recalled fact; the other form -> English name): separates a composition failure from a missing translation or symbol
memory → memory on the same contexts: it does not need the statements, so a drop there is damage from a foreign context, not a lookup failure
answer read vs 8-token greedy: validates the one-forward read the patching runs use
n: gate cuts (domain x form x family, main): 200 scenes each (>= 35); usable-scene count per (domain, form): up to 200; dev cells: 60 each. 2400 main + 1440 dev items, 21760 prompts
notes: Greedy, no sampling seeds; item seeds are alias_pointer_v1's (main 711, dev 712). Time from the measured rate of d3_competence_27b (17920 prompts of the same shape: 545 s generate + 454 s read on this A100, 17.9 prompts/s): 21760 prompts ~ 1210 s + model load ~ 0.4 h; 0.45 h with margin. The 0.8B smoke (qwen35_08b_smoke_alias_comp2, 3 items per file, 612 prompts, 6 s) checks the code path only. Needs scripts/alias_pointer_v1.py and data/alias_pointer_v1/ committed before enqueueing.

question: On pointer_v1's locker scenes (5 entities, animals and elements), when the last tokens before the answer cannot read the statement giving the answer, does memory → prompt still lose answer org, and does named → prompt (the entity named in the question) too; is the read in layers 48-63 and through attention layers, as on the animal scenes; and does memory → memory stay untouched?
why_it_matters: The first night found, on one animal wording, that the last tokens read the answer's statement themselves, through attention, in layers 48-63, where the bridge is in transit and the lens cannot write it (d2_ko_core_v1 / d2_ko_sweep_v1, UNVERIFIED). D3's pointer patching runs on these pointer_v1 scenes, so the read must be shown where D3 measures. named → prompt is the classic binding retrieval (no recall step): if it reads the statement at the same depth, the late read is the lookup itself, not something that waits for a recalled bridge.

hypotheses.H_late_read: memory → prompt and named → prompt each: the statement giving the answer hidden from the last tokens in all 64 layers keeps answer org <= 40% (NEEDED); hidden only in layers 48-63 <= 60% (NEEDED or PARTIAL); only in 0-31 or only in 32-47 >= 90%; in every attention layer <= 40% (NEEDED); in every DeltaNet layer >= 90%. Prior: memory → prompt 0.65 (animal scenes replicate), named → prompt 0.5
hypotheses.H_named_earlier: named → prompt already needs the statement in layers 32-47 (middle band NEEDED): with the entity named, the lookup can start earlier. Prior 0.3
hypotheses.H_question_free: both lookup families keep >= 90% with the statement hidden from the question words only (animal scenes: 100%). Prior 0.75
hypotheses.H_null: memory → memory: every cell >= 95% (animal scenes: 100%). Prior 0.9
hypotheses.positive_control: every lookup family with the statement hidden from everything after it and removed from the DeltaNet recurrence: <= 30% (5 lockers in the prompt: guessing gives ~20%)

Items: pointer_v1 main, domains animals and elements (the domains where all three families pass d3_competence_27b's gate: clean Wilson lower bound >= 0.85; months fails memory → prompt, planets fails memory → memory), scenes with every competence prompt right in all three families, first 100 per domain by scene id, and unedited read right. A cell is NEEDED if accuracy drops >= 20 points and the paired bootstrap 95% lower bound of acc(same-kind off-path statement) - acc(cell) >= 10 points; NOT NEEDED if the Wilson 95% lower bound of accuracy is >= 90%; else PARTIAL. "Late attention read" holds for a family iff all-layer NEEDED, every-attention-layer NEEDED, every-DeltaNet-layer accuracy >= 90%, layers 48-63 NEEDED or PARTIAL, and layers 0-31 and 32-47 each >= 90%. A family whose positive control is not NEEDED is not interpreted.
controls: a statement of the same kind off the answer's path (another entity's locker, same token length, seeded per scene): rules out "any statement-sized hole breaks the answer"
a random span of the same length inside the statements (never the answer's statement): rules out "any hole in the context"
the up to 3 tokens right after the statement (the DeltaNet conv's reach): what blocking them alone does
memory → memory on the same scenes (the answer is recalled): rules out generic damage to the last tokens
positive control: the statement hidden from everything after it and removed from the DeltaNet recurrence

n: 175 org prompts per family (animals 96 + elements 79 eligible scenes; every cut per (domain, family) has n >= 79 >= 35, so NOT NEEDED is reachable)
notes: Rows: 47,250 knocked reads (90 per item: 4 destinations x 4 sources at all layers, 4 sources x 2 destinations with the statement removed from the recurrence, and 11 layer sets (the three bands 0-31 / 32-47 / 48-63 each whole, attention-only and DeltaNet-only, every attention layer, every DeltaNet layer) x 2 destinations (last tokens, both) x 3 sources (the statement, the off-path control, the random span)). title: D3 code: can the 27B answer the Python-code lookups (key named, by list position, through variables, from a cue)?
command: uv run python scripts/code_pointer_v1.py manifest --set main dev --name code_competence_27b --why "D3 code gate: can the 27B run code_pointer_v1's Python lookups (key named, by list position, through a 2- or 3-variable chain, recalled from a cue) and the recall contrast, every alt prompt and each step alone, in chat format?" && uv run python scripts/code_pointer_v1.py competence --name code_competence_27b

question: Can Qwen3.6-27B answer code_pointer_v1's org prompts, the three alt prompts (dissoc, same, redigit) and each step alone, per domain (animals, months), family (named → prompt, list position → prompt, 2-variable chain → prompt, 3-variable chain → prompt, memory → prompt, memory → memory) and size (5 dict entries: all 400 scenes per domain; pilot: 3 and 8 entries, 60 scenes per cell, 8 entries for animals only)?
why_it_matters: Gate for the code version of the D3 dissociation patch (pointer_swap on data/code_pointer_v1/). The prose scenes ("The cow's locker is 5.") read as toy; code is where a pointer is literal (a list index, a variable naming a variable, a dict entry), so a "position" verdict there is the cleanest evidence for the pointer account of the "around" route (C2: the first night found the last tokens carrying the statement slot at 44-50 more often than the entity), and an "identity" or "value" verdict in code would bound it. The patching verdicts are interpretable only on items the model answers unedited, every alt prompt and step included; the list-position and variable-chain families and the dict-lookup-from-a-cue wording are untested on the 27B.

hypotheses.H-code-competent: named → prompt, list position → prompt and 2-variable chain → prompt: org prompt >= 95% in both domains at 5 entries (suite_v1 CODE, a two-dict lookup: 100%; pointer_v1 named → prompt: 100%); 3-variable chain → prompt >= 90%; >= 85% of their items eligible (every prompt right)
hypotheses.H-recall-lookup-animals: memory → prompt (animals) org-prompt Wilson lower bound >= 0.85 (pointer_v1's animals memory → prompt: 98%); memory → memory >= 95% in both domains (pointer_v1: 100%)
hypotheses.H-months-memory-lookup-fails: memory → prompt (months) org prompt < 85% (pointer_v1's months memory → prompt: 46% although each step alone was 100%): then months enter the patching runs without that family
hypotheses.H-more-entries-harder: at 8 entries list position → prompt and 3-variable chain → prompt lose >= 5 points against 5 entries (animals); at 3 entries every family within 2 points of 5
hypotheses.prior: Agent prior: H-code-competent 0.8 (most likely failure: 3-variable chain below 90%, or list position on months); H-recall-lookup-animals 0.75 (risk: "What number does lockers store for the animal known for mooing?" answered with the key, as the 0.8B smoke did); H-months-memory-lookup-fails 0.7; H-more-entries-harder 0.5.

decision_rule: A (domain, family) cell enters the code patching runs iff its org-prompt Wilson 95% lower bound >= 0.85 at 5 entries (suite_v1's rule; with n = 400 that needs >= 88% right); an item is eligible iff every prompt of it is right (org, dissoc, same, redigit, hop1, hop2). pointer_swap samples scenes eligible in all of a run's families, so a failing family is dropped from that domain's run rather than shrinking the others. The run is valid only if the answer read agrees with the 8-token greedy answer on >= 99% of prompts per cell. Pilot cells (3 and 8 entries) are reported and never gate a run.
controls: each step alone (hop1: the key alone, i.e. names[i], the chain's last variable, or cue -> key; hop2: the lookup with the key named, or the recalled fact): separates a composition failure from a missing step
named → prompt on the same scene (same dict line, same predictions): the reference every other family is read against
memory → memory on the same code (same dict, a recall question): competence with the code present but unused
answer read vs 8-token greedy: validates the one-forward read the patching runs use
n: Gate cut = one (domain, family) at 5 entries: n = 400 scenes (12 cuts, 4,800 items); pilot cuts n = 60 (18 cuts, 1,080 items, reported only); 33,320 prompts. The later patching runs sample from up to 400 checked scenes per domain, so a per-slot cut (5 slots) keeps n >= 35 for the same-control bound if >= 175 scenes per domain are eligible in all of a run's families.

title: D3b: does a fitted statement-slot direction steer the lookup where the lens push cannot?
command: uv run python scripts/pointer_fit.py run --name d3b_slot_direction_main_27b --why "D3b: fit a statement-slot direction at the tokens after the question (layers 40-52) on the fit scenes, steer held-out scenes with it at the alt-prompt patch's size, against the lens push, a random push, a shuffled-label direction and memory → memory items"
examples_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_fit.py examples --name d3b_slot_direction_main_27b
figures_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_fit.py figures --name d3b_slot_direction_main_27b
question: In memory → prompt on Qwen3.6-27B, does adding a direction fitted to "the asked statement is slot j" (minus the current slot) at the tokens after the question, layers 44-52, switch the answer to the digit at slot j, where the lens push (bridge alt − bridge org) of the same size does not?
why_it_matters: D3 found that at layers 44-50 the last tokens carry which statement slot is asked more often than which entity (29% vs 9%), and the lens cannot steer there. If a fitted slot direction steers the lookup, the "around" route is a statement pointer the model reads, outside the lens's word directions (supports C2's explanation); if it does not, D3's slot answers came from the whole patch, not a linear slot code.

hypotheses.H-slot: slot direction at layer 48, 1x: the answer at the target slot on >= 40% of memory → prompt items (Wilson lower bound >= 30%), lens push <= 10% and random <= 5% at the same size; shuffled-label direction <= 5%; memory → memory <= 5%; held-out entities within 15 points of seen ones; rank-4 subspace within 10 points of the full direction; slot decodable from the last tokens at 44-50 (5-way cross-validated accuracy >= 60%, chance 20%); slot directions no closer to the entities' lens word directions than random (largest |cos| at the null) and their lens-readable share at the random-dictionary null
hypotheses.H-no-linear-slot: slot direction <= 15% at every layer and size 0.5-2x (4x may only break answers); decodability may still be high (readable but not used)
hypotheses.H-illusion: the slot direction passes, but the remainder outside real activation differences alone reaches >= half of its rate while the in-span part stays below half, or the shuffled-label direction also moves >= 10%
hypotheses.prior: Agent prior: H-slot 0.35, H-no-linear-slot 0.5, H-illusion 0.15.

decision_rule: Fixed in scripts/pointer_fit.py's docstring and manifest. Primary cell: memory → prompt, animals and elements pooled, all held-out items, slot direction (per-token difference of class means, target minus current slot) at layer 48, 1x the alt-prompt patch's per-token size, added at every token after the question. "The slot direction steers the lookup where the lens push does not" iff (a) its rate of answers at the target slot has a Wilson 95% lower bound >= 0.30 and (b) it is >= 20 points above both the lens push and the random push at the same size, with each difference's paired-bootstrap 95% lower bound > 0. Valid only if the shuffled-label direction (memory → prompt) and the slot direction on memory → memory both keep their Wilson upper bound <= 0.10. Illusion flag reported with the verdict. Every other layer, size, subspace rank, the held-out-entity cut and the geometry are reported, not decisive.
controls: random push per token at the same size (rules out any push of that size)
lens push bridge alt − bridge org at the same size (the comparison the claim is about)
shuffled-label direction: the same fit with slot labels permuted (rules out a direction that works without slot information)
memory → memory items: no lookup, so a slot pointer should do nothing (rules out generic answer damage)
held-out scenes (main set; fit on the separate fit set) and held-out entities (queried entity never queried in the fit)
span of real activation differences vs the remainder, each added alone (Makelov et al. 2023 illusion check)
alt-prompt patch at the same tokens and layers (reference: D3's 29% slot answers)
n: memory → prompt: 175 held-out items (animals 96 + elements 79 eligible; >= 35 for every pooled cut, ~85 in the held-out-entity cut); memory → memory: 100 (50 per domain, >= 35); fit: up to 400 fit items, about half kept after the answered-right and fitting-half filters
notes: Timing from the measured A100 rate for the 27B (31-37 edited reads/s): memory → prompt 175 x (1 + 6 layer settings x (4 sizes x 11 conditions + 1 patch)) = 47.4k reads, memory → memory 100 x (1 + 6 x (4 x 4 + 1)) = 10.3k: ~57.7k reads ~ 28 min; + collect (400 forwards) and fit ~1 min, geometry ~2 min, load ~4 min, per-item overhead ~3 min: ~0.7 h. Layers 40-52 are past the first third of the depth. Results: results/pointer_fit/d3b_slot_direction_main_27b/.

controls: same entity, statements reshuffled: every hypothesis predicts answer org
random push of the same size; a prompt of the other topic, same size

question: On 5-statement scenes with one filler sentence of a statement's length, when the alt prompt's hidden states at the tokens after the question (and at the last two tokens) are patched into the org prompt at layers 40-60, does the org prompt answer the digit at the same statement ORDER (answer at the same statement slot) or at the same TOKEN position (answer at the same token position)? And is the late "alt prompt's own answer" more common when that digit is also in the org prompt (a pointer to the answer token) than when it is not (the digit carried as content)?
why_it_matters: The first night found that the tokens after the question carry the statement's slot at layers 44-50 (29% vs 9% for the word), but slot order and token position always coincided, and the alt answer was never in the org prompt. If the slot is an order index, the "around" route is a binding ID in the sense of the binding/lookback literature (positional pointers the word lens cannot express); if it is a token position, it is an attention address, closer to D2's finding that the last tokens read the statement through attention at 48-63. If the alt answer needs to be in the prompt, the late phase is a second pointer (reflexive), not the answer carried as a word: either way the lens could read but not write it.

hypotheses.H-order: memory -> prompt, after the question or last two tokens, at the layer of the slot peak (48-50): answer at the same statement slot >= 25% and answer at the same token position <= 10% (offset-shift scenes); verdict "position"
hypotheses.H-token: the same cells: same token position >= 25% and same statement slot <= 10%; verdict "token"
hypotheses.H-both: both >= 10% (verdict "mixed"): the pointer is partly positional in tokens, partly in order
hypotheses.H-reflexive: last two tokens, layers 52-56: the alt answer share with the digit in the org prompt minus without it >= +10 points (paired lower bound)
hypotheses.H-content: the same difference within ±10 points (CI): the digit is carried as content (v1: 98% alt answer at layer 56 though the digit was never in the org prompt)
hypotheses.prior: Agent prior: H-order 0.55, H-token 0.25, H-both 0.2; H-content 0.75, H-reflexive 0.25.

decision_rule: Fixed before the run (scripts/pointer_swap.py docstring, "Decision rule" and "pointer_v2 additions"). Per cell (family x patched tokens x layer or window x alt prompt), pooled over topics, Wilson 95%: interpretable iff the patch changes the answer (lower bound >= 0.20) and the 'same' control changes it rarely (upper bound <= 0.10); the verdict is the outcome whose lower bound exceeds the other candidates' upper bounds and the chance bar (the random push's upper bound, the per-digit rate of unpredicted context digits); offset-shift cells have the candidates {answer of bridge alt's statement, answer at the same statement slot, answer at the same token position, the alt prompt's own answer}. Primary cells: memory -> prompt, offset shift, after the question and last two tokens, layers 48 and 50 and the window 44-52. Reflexive: per cell, the paired (same scene) difference of the alt-answer share, reflexive minus plain, with a paired bootstrap 95% CI: 'reflexive' if the lower bound > +0.10, 'content' if the CI lies within ±0.10, else unclear; read only where the plain cell is interpretable. Every cut the rule is applied to needs n >= 35; cuts below are reported, not judged. A verdict holding in only one of the two topics is reported as topic-dependent.
controls: same entity, statements reshuffled (the "same" alt prompt): every hypothesis predicts answer org; rules out damage
random push of the same size (plain scenes, every 2nd layer of the list): the chance bar for each predicted digit
a prompt of the other topic, same size (plain scenes): realistic-activation null
context digits no hypothesis predicts: chance inside the same runs
plain scenes vs offset-shift scenes on the same org prompts: the slot answer should not move when only the filler moves (if it does, the order/token split is confounded by the filler)
org prompt into itself (no-op) and layer-0 all-position patch (reproduces the alt answer): hook checks
n: up to 180 scenes per topic (all eligible); per (topic x slot class x family x type) about 60 before the gate, expected ~54 (animals) and ~42 (elements) after it if the gate keeps 90% / 70% of scenes; pooled over topics ~96 per slot class and ~290 per family x type. The rule is applied to cuts with n >= 35 only.
notes: Reads per case: 3 checks + question words at 6 layers x 2 alt prompts + after the question and last two tokens at 17 layers x 2 x 2 + windows ((2 sites x 3) + 1) x 2 = 97 (offset, reflexive); plain scenes also get the random push and the other-topic patch at every 2nd layer of the list (3 for the question words, 9 for each other site) x 2 = +42, so 139; ~111 on average. ~1,730 cases (288 eligible scenes x 2 families x 3 types) -> ~192k reads; d3_main_ae_27b ran 92,100 reads in 2,401 s (38/s incl. forwards) -> ~85 min + load -> 1.5 h.

title: D3b: does the pointer direction mean "the Nth statement" or "this token position"?
command: uv run python scripts/pointer_order.py run --name d3b_order_vs_position_27b --why "D3b order or position: fit the pointer direction on pointer_v2 prompts whose asked statement precedes the filler sentence (the Nth statement = the Nth position), push held-out scenes toward a statement after the filler (the Nth statement now sits one position later), two folds"
examples_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_order.py examples --name d3b_order_vs_position_27b
figures_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_order.py figures --name d3b_order_vs_position_27b
question: When the pointer direction (fitted to "the question asks statement N") is pushed into a scene where a filler sentence has shifted the later statements by one position, does the model answer with the Nth statement's digit (ORDER) or with the digit of whatever statement now sits at position N (TOKEN POSITION)?
why_it_matters: d3b_slot_direction_main_27b found a direction that steers the lookup where the lens push cannot (37% vs 0%), but in pointer_v1 "the Nth statement" and "the Nth token position" are the same thing. ORDER means the "around" route is an ordinal pointer into a list (the binding-ID / lookback picture); TOKEN means it is a positional address, which would not survive any change of layout and points to attention-by-position, not to a variable.

hypotheses.H-order: statements after the filler, layer 48, 2x: answers = the target statement's digit >= 20%, = the digit now at its old position <= 5%; targets before the filler (both readings agree) >= 25%; read test (no push, asked statement after the filler): the fitted read-out picks the statement's number more often than the position one later
hypotheses.H-token: order <= 5%, token >= 20%; the read test picks the position one later
hypotheses.H-both: both >= 10% (the direction carries a mixture, or the two codes coexist)
hypotheses.H-no-transfer: targets before the filler < 15% (the direction does not work in these scenes): not interpretable
hypotheses.prior: Agent prior: H-order 0.45, H-token 0.3, H-both 0.15, H-no-transfer 0.1 (positional binding IDs in the literature are ordinal; but every context here has the same length, so a positional code would also have been sufficient for the model).

decision_rule: Fixed in scripts/pointer_order.py's docstring and manifest. Primary cut: memory → prompt, held-out scenes whose asked statement comes before the filler, targets after it (separating), slot push (target minus current) at layer 48, 2x the alt-prompt patch's per-token size. order = share of answers = the target statement's digit, token = share = the digit of the statement that now sits at the target's position; order - token by a scene-cluster bootstrap (2000, seed 0). ORDER iff order - token has its 95% lower bound > 0, order >= 2 x token and order's Wilson lower bound >= 0.10; TOKEN iff the reverse; BOTH iff both Wilson lower bounds >= 0.10 and neither; else inconclusive. Valid only if targets before the filler land on the target statement with Wilson lower bound >= 0.15, the random push and the shuffled-label direction land on either predicted digit with Wilson upper bound <= 0.10, and the slot push changes memory → memory answers with Wilson upper bound <= 0.10 (each n >= 35). Filler-position targets, scenes whose asked statement follows the filler, the push without the current statement, layer 44, 1x, both layers and the read test are reported, not decisive.
controls: random push per token at the same size (rules out any push of that size)
shuffled-label direction (rules out a direction that works without statement information)
memory → memory items: nothing is looked up, so a pointer should change nothing
targets before the filler: both readings agree there (positive control: the direction works in pointer_v2 at all)
targets at the filler's position: the order reading predicts the target digit, the token reading the filler (no digit)

push without the current statement (target minus the mean): neutral between the readings; the primary subtracts the current statement, which is the same under both readings only when it precedes the filler (hence the primary cut)
two folds: every scene is steered by a fit that never saw it
n: memory → prompt: 287 eligible scenes (animals 180, elements 107). Primary cut: 125 separating target instances in 55 scenes (animals 77, elements 48), >= 35; positive control 392 instances (122 scenes); memory → memory 287 scenes x 4 targets; read test 59 scenes whose asked statement follows the filler; fit 367 + 363 prompts (two folds)
notes: Timing: 287 memory → prompt scenes x 97 rows + 287 memory → memory x 49 = ~41.9k edited reads at 31-37/s ~19-23 min, + collect (~730 fit prompts and 2 forwards per scene) ~1 min, load ~4 min, overhead ~3 min: ~0.5 h. A stronger version needs a data change (see the agent report): a pointer_v2 fit set with the filler always last and a steer set with it always first, so every target after statement 1 separates the readings. Results: results/pointer_order/d3b_order_vs_position_27b/.

title: D3: is the statement-slot pointer counted from the start or from the end of the list (or is it a token position)?
command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py manifest --data pointer_v3 --set main --name d3_start_or_end_main --families RL DL --n 120 --layers 40 42 44 46 48 50 52 54 56 --groups final last --competence d3_start_or_end_competence_27b --why "D3 start or end: alt prompts with one statement more or fewer, so the slot counted from the start, the slot counted from the end and the same token position name three different org statements; animals and elements" && uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py run --name d3_start_or_end_main
examples_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py examples --name d3_start_or_end_main
figures_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py figures --name d3_start_or_end_main
question: When the alt prompt has one statement more (or fewer) than the org prompt and its hidden states at the last two tokens (and at every token after the question) are patched into the org prompt at layers 40-56, does the org prompt answer the digit of the statement at the same place counted from the START of the list, counted from the END, at the same TOKEN position, the answer of bridge alt's statement, or the alt prompt's own answer?
why_it_matters: The pointer found at layers 44-50 (the slot answer beats the word) could be an index from the start of the list (a binding ID as in the lookback literature), an index from the end (recency, as attention to the latest bindings), or an address in the token sequence. With equal list lengths all three coincided. Which one it is decides what a "pointer readout" must read, and whether the lens's failure to steer is about indices or about attention addresses.

hypotheses.H-start: memory -> prompt, last two tokens, layer 50 (and after the question, layer 48): answer at the same slot counted from the start >= 25% and counted from the end <= 10%, in both alt types
hypotheses.H-end: counted from the end >= 25% and from the start <= 10%, in both alt types
hypotheses.H-token: the same token position >= 25%, both slot answers <= 10% (would agree with a token-position result of d3v2_offset_reflexive_main)
hypotheses.H-mixed: two of them >= 10% (verdict "mixed"), or the winner differs between one more and one fewer
hypotheses.prior: Agent prior: H-start 0.4, H-token 0.25, H-end 0.15, H-mixed 0.2.

decision_rule: Fixed before the run (scripts/pointer_swap.py docstring, "Decision rule" and "pointer_v3 additions"). Per cell (family x patched tokens x layer or window x alt type), pooled over topics, Wilson 95%: interpretable iff the patch changes the answer (lower bound >= 0.20) and the same-entity control changes it rarely (upper bound <= 0.10); the verdict is the outcome among {answer of bridge alt's statement, slot from the start, slot from the end, same token position, the alt prompt's own answer} whose lower bound exceeds the others' upper bounds and the random push's upper bound; else "mixed". Primary cells: memory -> prompt, last two tokens and after the question, layers 48 and 50 and the window 44-52; the answer counts only if it holds for both alt types, else it is type-dependent. Every cut needs n >= 35; cuts below are reported, not judged.
controls: same entity, statements reshuffled (same filler places): every hypothesis predicts answer org
random push of the same size (every 2nd layer): chance bar for each predicted digit
a prompt of the other topic, same size: realistic-activation null
org prompt into itself (no-op) and the layer-0 all-position patch (hook checks)
both alt types: an artefact of one filler arrangement should not appear in both
n: up to 120 scenes per topic x alt type (all eligible): per (topic x alt type x family) ~115 (animals) and ~80 (elements) if the gate keeps 96% / 68% as for pointer_v2, i.e. >= 100 per topic pooled over the alt types; per alt type pooled over topics ~195. Slot cuts (first / middle / last, 40 each before the gate) fall below 35 for elements alone and are judged only pooled over topics.
notes: Reads per case: 3 checks + 9 layers x 2 sites x 2 (alt, same) + random/other at 5 layers x 2 sites x 2 + 3 windows x 2 sites x 2 = 71; ~790 cases (395 eligible scenes x 2 families) -> ~56k reads at 34/s -> ~28 min + forwards and load (~10 min) -> 0.7 h. title: D2 batch 3: in Python code, which later lines read the answer's dict entry? (the names list, each chain line, the print line, the last tokens, and their unions)
command: uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py manifest --name d2_code_readers --why "D2 batch 3 (b): the answer's dict entry hidden from one later code line at a time (names list, chain lines, print line, rest of the question, last tokens) and from unions with the last tokens, all layers, on code_pointer_v1 (animals, months)" --dataset code_pointer_v1 --families DK IX CH2 CH3 RK --domains animals months --n 100 --grid code_readers && uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py run --name d2_code_readers && uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py summarise --name d2_code_readers

figures_command: uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py figures --name d2_code_readers
question: In code_pointer_v1 (lockers = {"bee": 7, ..., "mouse": 5}; names = ["mouse", ...]; print(lockers[names[0]]) -> 5), batch 2 found (UNVERIFIED) that hiding the answer's dict entry from the last tokens in all layers leaves 36% of list-position programs right (43/120), from the question words (print line onward) 100%, from everything after the entry 3%. Which later lines read the entry themselves: the names list line, a chain line (x = "mouse"), the print line, the rest of the question? Does a line pass it on, i.e. does hiding it from that line and the last tokens together cost more than the last tokens alone, and do these lines account for the gap between 36% and 3%?
why_it_matters: The late read by the last tokens is D2's main finding; the 36% that survive it in list-position code say the entry also reaches the answer another way. If the names list line (which contains "mouse") reads the entry and relays it, the model pre-fetches values at the key's mention, a different mechanism from the late lookup, and the J-space question then applies to the list tokens, not only the last ones. The named-key family is the code analogue of named → prompt's early read at the question words (here: the key literal in the print line).

hypotheses.H_print_reader: named key: the print line (print(lockers["mouse"])) is a reader of the entry (batch 2: the question words, which start at the print line, are needed: 6% kept). Prior 0.8
hypotheses.H_list_not_reader: list position: the names list line alone is not a reader (the last tokens still read the entry directly). Prior 0.6
hypotheses.H_relay: list position: the names list line (or the print line) relays the entry: blocking it together with the last tokens costs >= 10 points more than the last tokens alone. Prior 0.65
hypotheses.H_explained: in every family, the union (last tokens + print line + list/chain lines + the rest of the question) keeps answer org within 10 points of hiding the entry from every line after the dict, i.e. no other line (the other chain, the closing fence) matters. Prior 0.55

decision_rule: Fixed before the run (scripts/attn_knockout.py BATCH3_RULES and INTERVALS, written into manifest.json). Items: code_pointer_v1 main, animals and months, the (domain, family) cells passing code_competence_27b's gate (clean Wilson lower bound >= 0.85; months fails it for the recalled key), scenes with every competence prompt right in every entered family, first 100 per domain by scene id, unedited read right. The entry is hidden (attention scores masked, DeltaNet values removed, all 64 layers) from: the names list line; each chain line by role (the key's chain, lines 1-3; the other chain); the print line; the rest of the question (closing fence, English question, instruction); the last tokens; the unions last tokens + print, + list/chain lines, + both, + both + the rest of the question; every line after the dict; everything after the entry. A line is a READER if acc(control) - acc(line) >= 10 points with the 95% entity-cluster bootstrap lower bound >= 5 points (control: another dict entry of the same token length hidden from the same line, same items). A line RELAYS if adding it to the last tokens' block costs >= 10 more points than the last tokens alone (entity-cluster lower bound >= 5). The lines EXPLAIN the survivors if the full union is within 10 points of "every line after the dict" (point estimate). Intervals: entity-cluster bootstrap (queried keys resampled within domain: 12 animals, 7 months; 4,000 draws, seed 0) first, item level second; every number per domain with n items / k keys. n per cut: 100 per domain (>= 35).
controls: another dict entry (same token length, seeded per scene) hidden from the same line or union: every reader and relay is measured against it
everything after the entry (the positive control of batch 2: 3% kept in list position)
the last tokens alone (reproduces batch 2: 36% in list position)

title: D5a: after a patch moves the lookup to another statement, does the late head (layer 51, head 22) look at the new statement? (and the J-lens's word, on the same tokens)
command: uv run python scripts/d5a_head_pointer.py manifest --name d5a_head_pointer_27b --why "D5a task b: does layer 51 head 22 (and the next 4 late heads) follow the pointer when pointer_swap's alt patch at layers 48 / 50 moves the answer, on d3v4_swap_main's pointer_v4 scenes; the J-lens's word read on the same tokens" --n 150 --families RL DL RR --competence d3v4_competence_27b && uv run python scripts/d5a_head_pointer.py run --name d5a_head_pointer_27b && uv run python scripts/d5a_head_pointer.py summarise --name d5a_head_pointer_27b

question: On unedited scenes layer 51 head 22 looks most at the asked statement from the last token (100% of held-out pointer_v1 scenes), but also on recall questions (95%), where the statement is not needed (d2_lookup_heads, UNVERIFIED). D3's patch of the alt prompt's last tokens / tokens after the question at layers 48 or 50 moves the answer to another statement of the org prompt (to the statement at the alt prompt's slot, or the alt entity's). Item by item: after the patch, does the head look most at the statement the new answer comes from (it follows the pointer), or still at the org prompt's asked statement (it tracks something the patch does not change)? Is that better than the J-lens's word read on the same tokens?
why_it_matters: D5a asks for a pointer read-out next to the J-lens, which reads the word but not the pointer. A head whose attention follows the patched pointer item by item would be that read-out (one head's attention, no fit) and would place the pointer in the head's query at layer 51; a head that stays on the asked statement would mean its 100% on unedited scenes reflects the bridge's identity or position in the context, not the lookup in progress. The recall control separates the two: there the answer moves without any lookup.

hypotheses.H_head_follows: memory → prompt, layer 51 head 22: on rows whose answer moved to another statement it looks most at the new answer's statement (entity-cluster lower bound >= 60%), and on rows whose answer stayed at the asked statement (lower bound >= 80%). Prior 0.5
hypotheses.H_head_static: it stays on the asked statement when the answer moves (lower bound >= 60%). Prior 0.35
hypotheses.H_head_beats_lens: on the same moved rows the head names the new statement more often than the J-lens's top entity at the last token (layer 50, what the head reads): paired entity-cluster lower bound > 0. Prior 0.6
hypotheses.H_controls: the same-entity patch and the random push change <= 10% of answers in each lookup family (d3v4_swap_main: 0% [0, 1] for both). Prior 0.9

decision_rule: Fixed before the run (scripts/d5a_head_pointer.py docstring "Decision rule", written into the manifest). Items: pointer_v4 main, d3v4_swap_main's scenes (pointer_swap.sample_cases, seed 0, n=150 per topic, eligible in every family by d3v4_competence_27b): countries, animals, body (85 queried entities, 9 wordings), families memory → prompt (primary), named → prompt (reference), memory → memory (recall control). Edits per item: the org prompt's block output at the last two tokens, or at every token after the question, replaced at layer 48 or at layer 50 by the alt prompt's (dissoc), the same-entity prompt's (same), or a random direction of the dissoc patch's per-position norm added (rand); one batched forward with the unedited row. Rows: per item and edit; outcome kept / slot / word / other statement / off the prompt by pointer_swap's role map; moved = slot, word or other statement, its new statement the org statement holding the new answer (memory → memory: the alt entity's statement). Reader: the statement with the most attention from the last token (summed over its tokens) for each listed head, recomputed from the edited forward; the J-lens: the top of the five entity tokens at the last token, block 50. Primary cut: memory → prompt, dissoc, the four settings pooled; intervals by entity cluster (queried entity resampled within topic, 4,000 draws, seed 0), Wilson second; judged only with >= 35 moved and >= 35 kept rows. H_head_follows: moved rows new statement lower bound >= 60% AND kept rows asked statement lower bound >= 80%. H_head_static: moved rows asked statement lower bound >= 60%. Else neither. The other 4 heads: the same numbers, no verdict.
controls: same-entity patch (the same entity at the same slot, the rest reshuffled): every hypothesis predicts no move; the head should stay on the asked statement
random push of the dissoc patch's per-position norm: no move
memory → memory (recall questions): the answer moves without a lookup; does the head move to the bridge's new statement anyway?
the J-lens's word read on the same tokens and rows (paired)
check.json: a self-patch (the org prompt's own state) leaves the logits unchanged; the answer roles agree with d3v4_swap_main on the same items and edits
n: 1,350 org prompts (150 scenes per topic x 3 topics x 3 families), 4 patch settings x 3 sources each; moved rows expected (d3v4_swap_main, memory → prompt): ~23% / 81% (last tokens, layer 48 / 50), ~35% / 32% (tokens after the question): ~770 moved rows of 1,800
